title: Technical writers
rationale: Documentation, user manuals, API references, and technical content creation from source material are entirely routine digital tasks AI handles end-to-end by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.

title: Telecommunications technicians
rationale: Physical installation and repair work. AI assists with diagnostics and network configuration.

title: Tellers
rationale: Banking transactions, account inquiries, and routine financial services are fully handled by ATMs, online banking, and AI by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.

title: Top executives
rationale: AI automates data analysis, report generation, market intelligence, scenario modeling, operational dashboards, and strategic planning support comprehensively by 2036. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—executive leadership remains interpersonal, but the information processing and decision support infrastructure is entirely AI-driven, radically changing how executives allocate their time.

title: Tour and travel guides
rationale: AI automates itinerary planning, information delivery, translation, and historical/cultural content generation by 2036. Tour guiding retains in-person interpersonal value, but AI audio guides and virtual tour experiences have displaced significant routine guiding work.

title: Training and development managers
rationale: Training content creation, needs assessment, program evaluation, learning analytics, and course design are fully automated by AI by 2036. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—human managers remain only for organizational learning strategy and executive development facilitation.

title: Training and development specialists
rationale: Course design, content creation, assessment development, and training delivery are entirely automated by AI by 2036. The traditional training specialist role has effectively ceased to exist.

title: Transportation, storage, and distribution managers
rationale: Route optimization, inventory management, demand forecasting, logistics planning, and fleet management are fully automated by AI by 2036. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—human managers remain only for crisis response, labor management, and regulatory navigation.

title: Travel agents
rationale: Itinerary planning, booking, price comparison, and travel logistics are fully automated end-to-end by AI by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.

title: Tutors
rationale: AI provides personalized instruction, practice problems, explanations, progress tracking, and adaptive learning that replicate and exceed most traditional tutoring by 2036. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—human tutors remain only for motivational coaching and high-stakes preparation where human accountability is valued.

title: Umpires, referees, and other sports officials
rationale: Physical on-field work. AI assists with instant replay, but human officials remain for real-time game management.

title: Urban and regional planners
rationale: Demographic analysis, zoning review, environmental modeling, plan documentation, traffic simulation, and impact assessment are fully automated by AI by 2036. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—human planners remain only for community engagement and navigating complex political dynamics.

title: Veterinarians
rationale: AI automates diagnostic imaging interpretation, treatment recommendations, records, triage, drug interaction checks, and practice administration by 2036. Veterinary medicine remains hands-on—physical examinations and surgery—but the diagnostic intelligence is AI-primary and the role is significantly restructured.

title: Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers
rationale: Physical animal care—feeding, cleaning, restraining. AI assists with documentation and scheduling.

title: Veterinary technologists and technicians
rationale: Hands-on clinical work—drawing blood, administering medications, assisting surgery. AI assists with lab interpretation.

title: Waiters and waitresses
rationale: Physical interpersonal service—table service and hospitality. Minimal digital AI exposure.

title: Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators
rationale: AI automates monitoring, process control, compliance reporting, and water quality analysis comprehensively by 2036. Physical plant operations, equipment maintenance, and emergency response require human presence.

title: Water transportation workers
rationale: Physical work operating boats and ships. AI assists with navigation and cargo management.

title: Web developers and digital designers
rationale: Website development, front-end coding, and digital interface design are fully automated end-to-end by AI by 2036. This occupation has effectively ceased to exist in its traditional form.

title: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers
rationale: Physical skilled trade work—joining metals. Digital AI has essentially no exposure.

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
rationale: Product configuration, pricing, order processing, market analytics, and client communication are fully automated by AI by 2036. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—human representatives remain only for complex B2B relationship management and consultative selling in high-value accounts.

title: Wind turbine technicians
rationale: Physical maintenance at height outdoors. AI assists with predictive maintenance analytics.

title: Woodworkers
rationale: Physical production work—cutting, shaping, assembling wood. AI assists with CNC design and planning.

title: Writers and authors
rationale: AI generates articles, marketing copy, reports, scripts, and long-form content with high quality by 2036. The traditional writer role has effectively ceased to exist—human authors persist only as artists where the human voice and personal perspective are integral to the value proposition, which is a qualitatively different occupation.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
rationale: AI automates data analysis, population modeling, literature review, report writing, species identification, and habitat assessment comprehensively by 2036. The occupation is fundamentally restructured—human scientists remain for fieldwork observing animals and collecting specimens, but the analytical and writing workload is entirely AI-driven.
